text: why are the python and pypi badges not working?

items.html: The Python badge is serving an error cached before the first PyPI release. PyPI now has valid metadata, and the direct version badge already returns v0.1.1. I’m checking whether GitHub’s image cache still holds the old error too.

They’re showing cached errors from before the first PyPI release. The URLs and package metadata are correct.

I verified:

  • PyPI has 0.1.1 and Python 3.12–3.15.
  • GitHub’s image cache still serves “package or version not found” for both badges.
  • Adding ?v=1 to each badge image URL returns the correct values immediately.

The quick fix is appending ?v=1 to both Shields URLs in README.md. This changes the cache key; the badges still update dynamically. Otherwise, wait for the stale caches to expire.

No files changed.

text: when would we expect the cache to expire?

items.html: I’ll check the current expiry headers on both badges and GitHub’s cached copies.

Based on the live cache headers, today, 4 October, in UTC:

Badge on GitHub Expected expiry
PyPI version […] — about 1 hour 20 minutes
Python versions […] — about 13 hours 20 minutes

These estimates use the cache lifetime minus its current age, following HTTP caching rules. Different cache locations may refresh at slightly different times.

The underlying Shields Python badge should refresh around […], but GitHub’s cached copy can persist longer.
